biblical_reference.note: In the New Testament, the name Peter (Greek: Πέτρος, Petros) is given to the apostle Simon Bar-Jonah, who was a fisherman by trade before Jesus called him to be a disciple. Peter was a key figure among the apostles and is traditionally considered to be the first Bishop of Rome and the founder of the Roman Catholic Church.
